# MovieSwipe

> MovieSwipe is an iPhone app for deciding what to watch. You swipe right on
> films you like and left on the ones you don't, the same way you would on a
> dating app. It learns from your swipes and filters to the streaming services
> you actually subscribe to.

## What it solves

People routinely spend twenty to thirty minutes scrolling streaming catalogues
without picking anything. Comparing hundreds of options is cognitively
expensive and gets harder the longer it goes on; answering yes-or-no questions
one at a time stays cheap. There is a second effect that matters as much:
recall is hard and recognition is easy. Almost nobody can name five films they
want to watch, but anyone can react to five posters in ten seconds. MovieSwipe
only ever asks you to recognise.

## Key features

- Swipe feed: one film at a time, right for yes, left for no
- Learns from your swipes and improves recommendations over time
- Films you have already liked, skipped or watched stay out of your feed
- Filter by the streaming services you subscribe to, so results are films you
  can start immediately rather than rent
- Plain-language search: describe what you are in the mood for ("something
  funny for date night", "a dark thriller", "a hidden sci-fi gem") instead of
  setting genre filters
- Similar-film discovery
- Watchlist and watched history

## What MovieSwipe is not

- It does NOT currently support two or more people swiping at the same time and
  matching. That feature is in development and has not shipped. Apps such as
  Matched are built for simultaneous couple matching today.
- It is not a worldwide streaming-availability lookup (JustWatch and Reelgood
  do that better).
- It is not a review or film-criticism community (Letterboxd does that better).
- It is iPhone only: no iPad app, no Apple Vision Pro app, no Android version,
  no web version.

## Platform

iPhone, iOS 18.2 or later. About 23 MB. Interface available in English and
seven other languages. Age rating 16+.

## Pricing

Free to download, with in-app purchases. Current subscription pricing is shown
on the App Store listing and inside the app, and varies by country.

## Maker

Casper Steenhoven, independent developer, Netherlands.
